newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt cement offer nine times oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: Egypt cement offer nine times oversubscribed.

text.p: A share offer in a new cement company in southern Egypt was nine times oversubscribed, one of the agents for the sale said on Tuesday.

"We sold 10.5 million shares in South Valley Cement Company (SVCC). The offer was nine times oversubscribed and investors got 12 percent of what they wanted to buy," Fathi Ashour of Banque Misr told Reuters.

Shares were offered at 10 pounds each in the flotation, which represents 30 percent of the firm's total equity. Individual investors had to apply for at least 50 shares, while institutions had a 1,000-share minimum.
Ashour said investors were paying for the shares they bought by instalments.
SVCC was established by the Egyptian Saudi Group for South Valley Projects and has an issued capital of 350 million pounds ($100 million) with total investments of 850 million.
The founders include Banque Misr, two British companies, a Saudi company and several individual Saudi businessmen as well as other individual shareholders.
SVCC founders said in March the company would have a production capacity of 1.4 million tonnes a year in the first stage.
They said the new plant would be set up in the Western Desert oasis of Kharga, some 550 km (340 miles) southwest of Cairo.

The cement plant would be well placed to supply construction sites associated with President Hosni Mubarak's scheme to irrigate at least 500,000 acres of land in the Western desert with water pumped in from the lake behind the Aswan High Dam.

Two other cement companies have recently said they will build plants, one of them in south Egypt. The cement sector is highly profitable in Egypt and cement firms are among the blue chips on the stock market.
